Slave Receive

This sample demonstrates the function of the master device sending data and the slave device receiving data using the I2S peripheral.

In this sample, I2S0 is configured as the master for data transmission, and I2S1 is configured as the slave for data reception.

Users can change the I2S pin configuration in the sample, whether to enable GDMA transfer, and other information through different macro configurations. For specific macro configurations, see Configurations.

Requirements

For requirements, please refer to the Requirements.

Wiring

Use jumper wires to connect P2_4 (BCLK) to P4_0 (BCLK), P2_5 (LRC) to P4_1 (LRC), P2_6 (DACDAT) to P4_3 (ADCDAT), and P2_7(ADCDAT) to P4_2 (DACDAT).

Configurations

  1. The following macro can be configured to enable or disable GDMA transfer of I2S data. 1 indicates using GDMA, 0 indicates not using GDMA.

    #define I2S_CONFIG_GDMA                   1                      /*< Set this macro to 1 to enable GDMA transfer. */

  2. The following macros can be configured to modify GDMA channel-related settings.

    // Set the following macros to modify the I2S GDMA TX Channel configurations.
#define TDM0_TX_GDMA_Channel_NUM          3
#define TDM0_TX_GDMA_Channel              GDMA_Channel3
#define TDM0_TX_GDMA_Channel_IRQn         GDMA0_Channel3_IRQn
#define TDM0_TX_GDMA_Channel_Handler      GDMA0_Channel3_Handler

// Set the following macros to modify the I2S GDMA RX Channel configurations.
#define TDM0_RX_GDMA_Channel_NUM          2
#define TDM0_RX_GDMA_Channel              GDMA_Channel2
#define TDM0_RX_GDMA_Channel_IRQn         GDMA0_Channel2_IRQn
#define TDM0_RX_GDMA_Channel_Handler      GDMA0_Channel2_Handler

  3. The following macro can be configured to modify the GDMA data transfer length.

    #define GDMA_TRANSFER_SIZE                200                     /*< Set this macro to modify the transfer size. */

  4. The following macros can be configured to modify pin definitions.

    #define I2S0_BCLK_PIN                     P4_0
#define I2S0_LRCK_PIN                     P4_1
#define I2S0_DATA_TX_PIN                  P4_2
#define I2S0_DATA_RX_PIN                  P4_3

#define I2S1_BCLK_PIN                     P2_4
#define I2S1_LRCK_PIN                     P2_5
#define I2S1_DATA_TX_PIN                  P2_6
#define I2S1_DATA_RX_PIN                  P2_7

Building and Downloading

For building and downloading, please refer to the Building and Downloading.

Experimental Verification

If the macro I2S_CONFIG_GDMA is set to 1:

  1. I2S0 uses GDMA to send data. After GDMA TX completes the data transfer, it enters the GDMA TX interrupt and prints a log.

    in gdma tx handler

  2. I2S1 uses GDMA to receive data. After GDMA RX completes the data transfer, it enters the GDMA RX interrupt and prints the received data.

    in gdma Rx handler
recv data [0]= 00000000
recv data [1]= 00000001
...
recv data [199]= 000000c7

If the macro I2S_CONFIG_GDMA is set to 0:

  1. I2S0 (Master) sends data to I2S1 (Slave). After the Slave side receives the data, it enters the interrupt function and prints the received data.

    length = xx
data[0] = 0x00000000
data[1] = 0x12348800
data[2] = 0x12348801
...
data[10] = 0x12348809
data[11] = 0x00000000
...

Code Overview

This section introduces the code and process description for initialization and corresponding function implementation in the sample.

Source Code Directory

The directory for project file and source code are as follows:

  • Project directory: sdk\samples\peripheral\i2s\i2s_slave_recv\proj

  • Source code directory: sdk\samples\peripheral\i2s\i2s_slave_recv\src

Initialization

The initialization flow for peripherals can refer to Initialization Flow in General Introduction.

  1. Call Pad_Config() and Pinmux_Config() to configure the PAD and PINMUX of the corresponding pins.

    void board_i2s_init(void)
{
   // master config
   Pad_Config(I2S0_BCLK_PIN, PAD_PINMUX_MODE, PAD_IS_PWRON, PAD_PULL_NONE, PAD_OUT_ENABLE,PAD_OUT_LOW);
   Pad_Config(I2S0_LRCK_PIN, PAD_PINMUX_MODE, PAD_IS_PWRON, PAD_PULL_NONE, PAD_OUT_ENABLE,PAD_OUT_LOW);
   Pad_Config(I2S0_DATA_TX_PIN, PAD_PINMUX_MODE, PAD_IS_PWRON, PAD_PULL_NONE, PAD_OUT_ENABLE,PAD_OUT_LOW);
   Pad_Config(I2S0_DATA_RX_PIN, PAD_PINMUX_MODE, PAD_IS_PWRON, PAD_PULL_NONE, PAD_OUT_ENABLE,PAD_OUT_LOW);
   Pinmux_Config(I2S0_BCLK_PIN, BCLK_SPORT0);
   Pinmux_Config(I2S0_LRCK_PIN,  LRC_SPORT0);
   Pinmux_Config(I2S0_DATA_TX_PIN,  DACDAT_SPORT0);
   Pinmux_Config(I2S0_DATA_RX_PIN,  ADCDAT_SPORT0);
   // slave config
   Pad_Config(I2S1_BCLK_PIN, PAD_PINMUX_MODE, PAD_IS_PWRON, PAD_PULL_NONE, PAD_OUT_ENABLE, PAD_OUT_LOW);
   Pad_Config(I2S1_LRCK_PIN, PAD_PINMUX_MODE, PAD_IS_PWRON, PAD_PULL_NONE, PAD_OUT_ENABLE, PAD_OUT_LOW);
   Pad_Config(I2S1_DATA_TX_PIN, PAD_PINMUX_MODE, PAD_IS_PWRON, PAD_PULL_NONE, PAD_OUT_ENABLE, PAD_OUT_LOW);
   Pad_Config(I2S1_DATA_RX_PIN, PAD_PINMUX_MODE, PAD_IS_PWRON, PAD_PULL_NONE, PAD_OUT_ENABLE, PAD_OUT_LOW);

   Pinmux_Config(I2S1_BCLK_PIN, BCLK_SPORT1);
   Pinmux_Config(I2S1_LRCK_PIN,  LRC_SPORT1);
   Pinmux_Config(I2S1_DATA_TX_PIN,  DACDAT_SPORT1);
   Pinmux_Config(I2S1_DATA_RX_PIN,  ADCDAT_SPORT1);
}

  2. Call RCC_PeriphClockCmd() to enable the I2S clock.

  3. Execute I2S_StructInit() and I2S_Init() to initialize the I2S master peripheral. The initialization parameters for I2S0 are configured as follows:

    1. Define a I2S_InitTypeDef type I2S_InitStruct, call I2S_StructInit() to pre-fill I2S_InitStruct with default values.

    2. Modify the parameters of I2S_InitStruct as required. The initialization parameter configuration for I2S Master is shown in the table below. Call I2S_Init() to initialize the I2S Master peripheral.

  1. Execute I2S_StructInit() and I2S_Init() to initialize the I2S slave peripheral. The initialization parameters for I2S1 are configured as follows:

    1. Define a I2S_InitTypeDef type I2S_InitStruct, call I2S_StructInit() to pre-fill I2S_InitStruct with default values.

    2. Modify the parameters of I2S_InitStruct as required. The initialization parameter configuration for I2S Slave is shown in the table below. Call I2S_Init() to initialize the I2S Slave peripheral.

  1. If the macro I2S_CONFIG_GDMA is set to 0, configure the I2S1 RX to prepare to receive data with the I2S_INT_RX_READY interrupt.

    #if (I2S_CONFIG_GDMA == 0)
   I2S_INTConfig(I2S1, I2S_INT_RX_READY, ENABLE);
   ...
#endif

  2. If the macro I2S_CONFIG_GDMA is set to 1, then GDMA initialization is required.

    1. Define a GDMA_InitTypeDef type GDMA_InitStruct, execute GDMA_StructInit() to pre-fill GDMA_InitStruct with default values.

    2. Modify the parameters of GDMA_InitStruct as required. The initialization parameter configuration for GDMA TX and RX channels is shown in the table below. Execute GDMA_Init() to initialize the GDMA peripheral.

    3. Configure the GDMA total transfer completion interrupt: GDMA_INT_Transfer and NVIC. For NVIC-related configurations, refer to Interrupt Configuration.

Functional Implementation

I2S Using GDMA for Data Transfer

In the case of using GDMA to transfer data with I2S, the macro I2S_CONFIG_GDMA needs to be configured to 1.

  1. Enable the I2S Slave RX function, enable the I2S Slave GDMA RX channel transmission, enable the I2S Master TX function, and enable the I2S Master GDMA TX channel transmission.

    I2S_Cmd(I2S1, I2S_MODE_RX, ENABLE);
GDMA_Cmd(TDM0_RX_GDMA_Channel_NUM, ENABLE);
I2S_Cmd(I2S0, I2S_MODE_TX, ENABLE);
GDMA_Cmd(TDM0_TX_GDMA_Channel_NUM, ENABLE);

    1. After enabling the I2S Master GDMA TX channel transmission, the GDMA TX channel transfers data from GDMA_Send_Buf to (&(I2S0->I2S_TX_FIFO_WR_ADDR)). When the length of the transferred data equals the set GDMA_BufferSize, it triggers the GDMA_INT_Transfer interrupt. Within the interrupt function, print the relevant information and clear the interrupt flag.

    void TDM0_TX_GDMA_Channel_Handler(void)
{
   DBG_DIRECT("in gdma tx handler");
//    GDMA_SetSourceAddress(TDM0_GDMA_Channel, (uint32_t)(&(I2S0->REG_I2S_TX_FIFO_0_WR)));
//    GDMA_SetDestinationAddress(TDM0_GDMA_Channel, (uint32_t)(&(I2S1->REG_I2S_RX_FIFO_0)));

   GDMA_SetBufferSize(TDM0_TX_GDMA_Channel, GDMA_TRANSFER_SIZE);

   GDMA_ClearINTPendingBit(TDM0_TX_GDMA_Channel_NUM, GDMA_INT_Transfer);
   GDMA_Cmd(TDM0_TX_GDMA_Channel_NUM, DISABLE);
}

  3. Enable the I2S Slave GDMA RX channel transfer. When the I2S Slave receives data, the GDMA RX channel moves the data from (&(I2S1->I2S_RX_FIFO_RD_ADDR)) to GDMA_Recv_Buf. When the length of the transferred data equals the set GDMA_BufferSize, it triggers the GDMA_INT_Transfer interrupt. In the interrupt function, print the received data information and clear the interrupt flag.

    void TDM0_RX_GDMA_Channel_Handler(void)
{
   DBG_DIRECT("in gdma Rx handler");
//    GDMA_SetSourceAddress(CODEC_GDMA_Channel, (uint32_t)(&(I2S0->REG_I2S_RX_FIFO_0)));
//    GDMA_SetDestinationAddress(CODEC_GDMA_Channel, (uint32_t)(&(UART5->RB_THR)));

   GDMA_SetBufferSize(TDM0_RX_GDMA_Channel, GDMA_TRANSFER_SIZE);

   GDMA_ClearINTPendingBit(TDM0_RX_GDMA_Channel_NUM, GDMA_INT_Transfer);
   for (uint32_t i = 0; i < GDMA_TRANSFER_SIZE ; i++)
   {
      DBG_DIRECT("recv data [%d]= %x", i, GDMA_Recv_Buf[i]);
   }

   GDMA_Cmd(TDM0_RX_GDMA_Channel_NUM, DISABLE);
}

I2S Does Not Use GDMA for Data Transfer

When I2S does not use GDMA for data transfer, you need to configure the macro I2S_CONFIG_GDMA to 0.

  1. After initialization is complete, enable the I2S Slave RX and I2S Master TX functions respectively. Execute I2S_SendData() in a loop 10 times to send 10 pieces of data.

    I2S_Cmd(I2S1, I2S_MODE_RX, ENABLE);
I2S_Cmd(I2S0, I2S_MODE_TX, ENABLE);

uint32_t i = 0x12348800;
for (uint16_t t = 0; t < 10 ; t++)
{
    if (I2S_GetTxFIFOFreeLen(I2S0))
    {
        /* 16bit format, lower half word send first! */
        I2S_SendData(I2S0, i++);
    }
}

  2. When the I2S Slave RX FIFO has data, it triggers the I2S_INT_RX_READY interrupt. In the interrupt handler, execute I2S_GetRxFIFOLen() and I2S_ReceiveFIFOData() to receive data.

    uint8_t len = I2S_GetRxFIFOLen(I2S1);
DBG_DIRECT("length = %d", len);
for (uint8_t i = 0; i < len; i++)
{
    DBG_DIRECT("data[%d] = 0x%X", i, I2S_ReceiveFIFOData(I2S1));
}
I2S_ClearINTPendingBit(I2S1, I2S_INT_RX_READY);
